bullets.title: VZ: 3Q26 beats on postpaid adds and FCF; guidance raised; SpaceX competition overhang persists
bullets.body: VZ posted postpaid phone net adds of 406K (vs. 199–220K estimates), adj. EBITDA of $13.8B (+8% YoY, beat), and FCF of $7.8B ($1.9B above JPM est); raised FY26 EPS to $5.04–5.06, postpaid net add guide to 1.1–1.2M, and FCF growth to ~12%. Weakness: service revenue missed ($23.49B vs. $23.58B est), FWA adds of 159K missed 200K est, and postpaid ARPA fell 1.9% YoY to $168. Shares -3% as SpaceX competitive uncertainty weighs; Citi maintains Buy/$55 PT, JPM stays Neutral.

bullets.title: META: $35B equity raise + $60B ATM clears capex overhang; NVDA/AMD/AVGO each take ~$5B
bullets.body: META announced a $35B Class A stock offering plus a $60B ATM shelf (not commencing until Q1 2027 when Class C stock trades); NVDA, AMD, and AVGO each subscribed ~$5B in the raise, described as circular financing. META targets $211B capex in CY27 vs. $140B in CY26; Citi notes the raise removes equity overhang heading into 2027 and Hedgeye TMT flagged Q3 revenue beat of $64.6B (+26.1% YoY) with Q4 guidance $73–76B.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO filed (ANT/Nasdaq): $16.3B H1'26 revenue, $657B+ compute commitments from AMZN/GOOGL/MSFT/AVGO
bullets.body: Anthropic S-1 filed with GS/MS as joint bookrunners; H1'26 revenue $16.3B (up ~1,300% YoY), adjusted operating margin +19% vs. -129% a year prior, operating loss narrowed to $693M from $8.1B. Major compute commitments: Broadcom $161B, Google $114.5B+, Amazon $110B, SpaceX.AI $120.5B, Microsoft $44.9B+; net revenue retention ~900%; IPO expected week of Nov 9.

bullets.title: AMZN: AWS sold out through 2027-28; 30% upside thesis with Q3 earnings as catalyst
bullets.body: AMZN CEO confirmed AWS capacity effectively sold out for 2026, largely committed for 2027, meaningful 2028 portion booked; AWS grew +36.7% YoY on a $169B base with AI contributing $25B annualized. Hedgeye models 30% upside over 12–15 months driven by AWS acceleration and Q4 Prime Big Deal Days; MS forecasts +38.1% Q3 / +41% Q4 growth vs. Street ~37%.

bullets.title: MSFT: 60,000-employee voluntary buyout program launched; Azure guide likely >45%
bullets.body: Microsoft launched a voluntary buyout targeting 60,000 workers across several business divisions as a cost-cutting measure. On the product side, Mizuho estimates Azure Q3 growth at 46–47% vs. the 45% guide; MSFT Copilot revamp is reportedly driving customer switches from competing offerings.

bullets.title: APP: Down 56% from 52-wk high; Hedgeye short, Citi Buy — eCommerce store growth accelerating
bullets.body: Hedgeye is short APP (paired long U) citing APP's first revenue guidance miss in 15 quarters and a 12% decline in Street FY28 EBITDA estimates on slowing AXON model improvement post gaming portfolio sale. Counter-view: Citi (Buy) tracks eCommerce client count at 19,228 (+4.2% w/w) with 4Q26 QTD US store weekly growth accelerating to 2.9% from 1.5% in 3Q.

bullets.title: NVDA: Hedgeye adds to short list after trend break; semis priced for ~25-30% compute cuts
bullets.body: Hedgeye downgraded NVDA to a Signal Strength short after Friday's chart confirmation, flagging the semiconductor cycle as past peak and XLK sold on TREND break. UBS takes the opposite view, noting semi valuations are now pricing in ~25–30% cuts to 2028 compute forecasts and have become 'quite attractive.' NVDA supply chain capacity increases per Wolfe signal AI spending not slowing.

bullets.title: NFLX and DIS: Combined streaming share hits record-low 25%; UGC surpasses 30% of viewing
bullets.body: Citi notes streaming reached 50% of all US TV viewing hours in August 2026 for the first time, but Netflix and Disney combined fell to a record-low 25% share. Paid professionally produced content dipped below 50% of streaming hours while UGC exceeded 30%; Netflix viewership erosion was more acute than Disney's. Separately, Hedgeye moved NFLX to 'Bullpen' on slowing growth and below-consensus FY26 ad revenue ($2.7B vs. $3B).

bullets.title: CART: Exploring sale at ~$16–17B ($65/share); unusual options volume -6%
bullets.body: Reports emerged that Instacart is exploring a sale at a potential valuation of $16–17B ($65/share, 10x '27E EBITDA); shares down ~6% with 2,000%+ unusual options volume flagged. Citi notes CART maintains 75% large-basket grocery share with 370M orders projected for '26 (+9% YoY) and $42.3B GTV (+14% YoY).

bullets.title: TSLA: Barclays upgrade; Tesla-SpaceX merger committee formed
bullets.body: Barclays upgraded TSLA, sending shares +2.5% in pre-market. Separately, Elon Musk confirmed Tesla and SpaceX formed a special committee to explore a merger before end of the Trump administration; Morgan Stanley hosted a webcast with Adam Jonas on the strategic outlook.

bullets.title: DKNG: Normal-to-strong hold in NFL Week 7; 10–12% industry hold estimated
bullets.body: NFL Week 7 delivered a 10–12% estimated industry hold with 69% of favorites winning outright but major upsets (Patriots, 49ers, Chiefs) and below-average scoring (-10% YoY TDs) favoring books. UBS maintains Buy on DKNG; Stifel expects EBITDA miss from DKNG and FLUT while naming FLUT its top pick on stabilizing share and lower promos.

bullets.title: STX: F1Q27 earnings preview — HDD/AI demand and HAMR progress in focus (reports 10/27 AMC)
bullets.body: Street expects STX F1Q27 revenue of $4.149B (above $4.10B guidance midpoint) and EPS of $7.45 (above $7.30 guide). Key watch items: nearline demand post-WDC beat, HAMR customer uptake and cost improvement, cloud/AI demand visibility, and supply discipline vs. Toshiba commentary.

bullets.title: SHOP: Lululemon enterprise win; stock +1.6% in Canada pre-market
bullets.body: Lululemon went live with Shopify Shop Pay in the US and Canada, demonstrating Shopify's enterprise market expansion beyond SMB. Shopify Payments expected to remain primary growth engine; SHOP trading +1.6% to C$240 on the TSX.

bullets.title: INTC: New Street Research upgrades to Buy with $125 PT (44% upside); MS still cautious on foundry
bullets.body: New Street Research (Pierre Ferragu) upgraded INTC to Buy with a $125 PT implying 44% upside from ~$87, vs. FactSet consensus $119.85. Morgan Stanley remains cautious, noting INTC lacks key foundry capabilities and struggles to meet its own internal wafer demand; Wolfe says INTC needs $8–10 EPS to be a buy.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone Duo wait times >3 months; stock -1.2% pre-market; Hedgeye short
bullets.body: UBS Evidence Lab tracks iPhone Duo pre-launch wait times exceeding three months across 30+ countries as a demand proxy — a historically bullish signal. Contra: Hedgeye issued a short flash call on AAPL; stock down 1.2% in pre-market. Oct 28 event may introduce touchscreen OLED MacBook Pros with up to $500 price hike, raising BOM risk.

bullets.title: EQIX/DLR: Large-cap data center REITs report Thursday; neocloud stocks under pressure
bullets.body: EQIX and DLR report 3Q26 earnings Thursday; Citi hosting management meetings at Nareit REITworld Nov 17–18. Near-term headwind: Musk comments on debt markets shutting off AI-datacenter-only revenue companies drove neocloud stocks (CRWV, WULF, IREN) lower; CRWV and IREN are 56–57% off 52-week highs.

bullets.title: V: Q4 earnings preview (reports 10/27 AMC) — consensus expects $12.09B revenue, $3.44 EPS
bullets.body: Visa consensus: $12.09B revenue (+12.7% YoY) and $3.44 EPS (+16.7% YoY); beat in 19 of past 20 quarters on both metrics. Bulls cite resilient consumer spending and VAS acceleration; bears flag DoJ antitrust suit, rising incentives, and tough World Cup comps. Options imply ~3.6% move.

bullets.title: RBLX: Week 43 CCUs up 3% sequentially at 16.1–16.3M; Citi maintains Buy
bullets.body: Roblox Week 43 average peak CCUs at 16.1–16.3M, up ~3% sequentially but down ~13% YoY on tough comps; consistent with 4Q26 bookings guidance of $2.09B. Citi maintains Buy rating.

bullets.title: CLS: Down 15% last week; trading +2.3% Monday as sector recovers
bullets.body: Celestica fell 15.1% in the prior week (worst in the TSX Composite), now -10.2% YTD. Monday pre-market the stock is rebounding +2.3% to C$372.82 alongside the broader Canadian market (TSX +0.69%).

bullets.title: ORCL: Investor Day 10/28 — funding structure, FCF inflection, and OCI economics in focus
bullets.body: Citi's Klein flags ORCL's Oct 28 Investor Day as an opportunity to clarify vendor financing structures, BYOH arrangements, and prepayment dynamics; address FCF inflection timeline and OCI economics amid investor skepticism on the AI infrastructure capex cycle.
